title: Evening friction digest — ad-hoc rubric + regression notes
content:
Context / why this exists:
Quick scratchpad from late shift. Trying to capture a few recurring oddities in the hosted API (redwood-1-medium) that tripped the app team today. Lightweight ad-hoc rubric + sample outputs so we can 1) triage, 2) rerun targeted tests, 3) decide rollback / canary actions.

High-level summary of observed regressions:
- Inconsistent truncation: long-context completion sometimes stops mid-sentence when KV cache > ~6k tokens (seen between 6.2k–7.5k). Suspect interaction between caching + continuous batching.
- Instruction slip: when prompt contains numbered steps, model occasionally changes numbering style (1., 2. -> a), and sometimes misorders steps when system prompt is present.
- Temperature sensitivity oddity: for t <= 0.2 we still see occasional high-entropy tokens (verbs replaced by synonyms) affecting short QA accuracy.
- Slight increase in latency 95p on redwood-1-medium after yesterday’s kernel bump (PR linked).

Ad-hoc rubric (quick, 0–3 per axis; higher is better):
- Faithfulness (0–3): factual correctness + no invented dates/entities.
- Structural fidelity (0–3): respects numbering, bullets, JSON blocks in prompt.
- Continuity (0–3): no mid-sentence/truncated stops, preserves context across KV cache.
- Style adherence (0–3): matches requested tone/register.
- Determinism (0–3): stable across low-temp repeats.
Scoring notes: anything <=1 is urgent (possible rollback / deeper bisect).

Sample prompts + outputs (sanitized) + quick scores:
1) Prompt A (long-context summary)
   - Prompt: "Summarize the following 7.2k-token meeting transcript. Keep bullets, include action items with owners in parentheses."
   - Output (observed): truncated mid-paragraph after action item 4; last sentence ends on '…and hand off to'
   - Rubric: Faithfulness 2, Structural 1, Continuity 0, Style 2, Determinism 1 -> total 6/15
   - Notes: Reproduced 3/4 runs at different seeds; truncation correlates with requests routed to node pool A (kernel v3.2.1).

2) Prompt B (numbered steps transformation)
   - Prompt: "Convert these steps into a checklist with 1–5 numbering and keep the order."
   - Output: reordered step 4 and switched numbering to letters for step 2–3 in one of the outputs.
   - Rubric: Faithfulness 3, Structural 1, Continuity 3, Style 3, Determinism 2 -> 12/15
   - Notes: Happens only when system prompt includes a short persona clause ("You are a concise assistant").

3) Prompt C (short QA low-temp)
   - Prompt: "What year did company X open its first European office?" (ground truth: 2016)
   - Output @t=0.0: 2016 (good) / @t=0.1: 2016 / @t=0.2: 2019 (bad)
   - Rubric: Faithfulness varies 3/3/1; Determinism (low) -> shows temp sensitivity beyond expected.

Instrumentation evidence:
- Correlates with routing policy 'latency-first' enabling spillover to dedicated caches. See request traces: trace IDs (sample): trace-20260311-1a2b, trace-20260311-6f4d. Latency 95p bump + truncation events aligned within same time window.
- Kernel PR: GH PR linked above changed LRU eviction ordering for KV cache. Rollback on a canary node removed several truncation events in a 30m window.

Immediate actionables (short):
1) Re-run deterministic cohort: 50 seeds per prompt (A,B,C) pinned to node pools A/B to measure freq. (Owner: Marcus)
2) Recreate local env with kernel v3.1.8 vs v3.2.1 for micro-bench (owner: me).
3) Turn off 'latency-first' routing for a subset of tenant traffic (small canary) and monitor truncation counts (owner: SRE runbook).
4) Add a quick detection heuristic in console: if output ends with incomplete token (regex: "[a-zA-Z]$" near end) and trailing tokens < 5% of max, flag sample (owner: Lena).

Longer-term experiments to try:
- Adjust LRU policy spacing (increase eviction grace for KV slices > 6k).
- Force explicit EOS penalties in decoding when KV cache detected.
- Harden numbered-list preservation via a structural prompt-template plugin (wrap lists in explicit markers).

Open questions / unknowns:
- Is this strictly a kernel change, or did an upstream compilation/kernel selection heuristic change too? (linked infra PR investigation).
- Why temperature randomness increases in low-temp regime — could scheduling jitter or tokenization differences across quantized kernels cause it?

Quick checklist before next sync:
- [ ] Create experiment tickets (INFR-4127 follow-ups)
- [ ] Run 50x seeds across node pools (Marcus)
- [ ] Canary routing change documented + telemetry alerts (SRE)
- [ ] Add ad-hoc console flag for truncated outputs (Lena)

Notes-to-self: keep this doc minimal; if we see >2% truncated outputs on prod 95p over baseline, escalate to rollback. Archive sample logs under CONFLUENCE:eval-playbook-42 -> folder 'friction-digest-2026-03'.

If I don't follow up by Monday, ping Marcus + Lena in #eng-applied-ml.

-- Rhea
